conbody.p: Calendar, above the chart, also says how the plan is scheduled.

strow.stentry: Tasks stay where they are put until you recalculate. This is how every plan starts
After every change, each task is placed from its relationships and its constraint
An automatic task starts no earlier than this day
Float is counted to this day, and goes negative for work that runs past it
Automatic tasks go as late as their float allows, not as early

conbody.p: A task can go its own way: under Scheduling in its panel, set its Mode to manual in an automatic plan, or automatic in a manual one.

An automatic task goes straight after the tasks that drive it. A task that nothing drives stays where you put it: type a start, or drag its bar, and it is held to start no earlier than that day, so the next change does not put it back.
A constraint holds a task to a date:

strow.stentry: Goes as late as its float allows
Start no earlier than, finish no earlier than
Cannot be placed before the date
Start no later than, finish no later than
Loses float as it nears the date, and is flagged past it
Must start on, must finish on
Is placed on the date, whatever drives it

conbody.p: A manual task is not moved by its constraint until you recalculate; until then its panel says when its dates do not keep to it.

The same section shows what the plan works out for the task: the earliest it can run (after the tasks that drive it, the plan's start and its constraint), the latest it can run before the plan ends later, and its float. Float is negative, shown as N working days behind, when a task runs past its deadline, a "no later than" constraint or the plan's finish date, or when a relationship it drives is broken; such a task is critical.
Tick A critical path for each chain of tasks in the calendar to give every independent chain its own path, to its own last task, where the default is one path to the end of the plan.
